name: Pad Woon Sen

ingredients.name: spring onion, cut into short lengths

steps: Soak dry mung bean glass noodles in room-temperature water for 8–10 minutes until flexible; drain and snip a few times with scissors. They finish cooking in the pan, so do not boil them first. Mix mushroom sauce, soy sauce, sugar, white pepper and measured 100 ml water.
Press the tofu dry. Heat 15 ml oil in a wide skillet and sear tofu cubes for 2–3 minutes per side until golden. Remove to a plate, leaving the pan hot.
Add remaining 20 ml oil, garlic and onion; fry 1 minute. Add carrot and cabbage and stir-fry 2–3 minutes until just starting to soften. Add tomato wedges and cook 1 minute so they keep their shape.

Add drained glass noodles and pour over the sauce. Lift and toss for 2–4 minutes until the noodles turn transparent, absorb most of the liquid and are chewy rather than hard. Add a small splash of water only if they dry before cooking through.
Return tofu and add the spring onion. Toss for a final minute to heat everything evenly. Divide immediately among four plates while the glass noodles remain springy and the vegetables retain color.
tips: Choose mung bean starch glass noodles; rice vermicelli looks and behaves differently. The reviewed photo shows transparent noodles, tofu, cabbage, carrot, tomato and spring onion without egg or meat.
notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.
